answer: Make every rewarded claim pass a stranger's rebuild: a randomly chosen outsider must recreate the result from the public record alone, with no help from its author. A hollow claim collapses on rebuilding, shifting like a dune under a second footstep and exposing the same shortcut every time it is copied. One operator cloning one piece of work across a hundred identities fails a hundred independent rebuilds, while genuine work, rooted like a juniper, survives because it was real the first time.
